summary: Finnish-Canadian garment magnate Peter Nygard built a clothing empire on exploited factory labor, then for decades allegedly lured women and girls to his Bahamas compound and abused them until his 2020 arrest.

evidence.note: born in Helsinki; family later emigrates to Winnipeg after the war
1967 buys into a women's garment maker that becomes his company
trafficked guest workers at a Jordanian factory sewing his pants
post-NAFTA Mexican factories: low wages, forced overtime, pregnancy tests
anti-union campaign and labor board ruling at his Manitoba plants
1980 rape charge in Winnipeg and 1990s harassment complaints
minors reported at his compound parties by a visiting actress
smear campaign against Bacon: paid protests, websites, journalists
FBI charges, Toronto charges, compound seized; in custody at release

notes: Nygard was alive and in custody at release, so covered_span ends at 2022. main_span runs from the 1967 company purchase to the 2020 arrest. Environmental damage from dredging at the compound gets a short segment, too brief for a theme. Secondary theme child-abuse added because several plaintiffs were 14 at the time.
